source.title: SPICE: Simple Polysemantic Feature Interpretation via Clustering-based Explanation
source.authors: Sehyun Lee; Dahee Kwon; D. Lee; Jaesik Choi

page_placements.theme: Architecture and training-time constraints (activation or weight sparsity, LWTA/TopK, decorrelation, concept supervision, gating, activation function, weight decay, non-negativity, write-disjoint experts, ViT vs ResNet) change neuron monosemanticity

record.file_problem: The paper and supplementary material are present. Some figure text is garbled, but the relevant tables and prose are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses attribution clustering and multimodality measures to analyze neuron-level polysemanticity across vision architectures. It tests architectural differences relevant to V4, but does not measure the claimed share of interpretable neurons.
record.gate_note: The study does not audit Qwen3-32B or report percentages of neuron poles with one or two jobs. Its results relevant here concern architectural differences in visual-model concept clusters and attribution-similarity distributions. Baseline separability scores are not included as results for V4 because they measure clustering-method performance, not the share of interpretable neurons. Cited findings are excluded.
record.test_reason: SPICE is a method paper. It takes vision-neuron polysemanticity as given, citing superposition, and mainly reports its own clustering method's separability and coverage against PURE, LE and CPE. Its depth and architecture analyses use Dip-test p-values of attribution-similarity distributions and SPICE cluster counts per neuron. These are properties of the tool's input and output, not a share of neurons with one main job. SPICE also yields clusters for 100/100 neurons by construction (Table 3), so the counts cannot be read as an interpretable-neuron share. The study has no language models, no InceptionV1 cat/car case, no attribution graphs, and no held-out firing prediction or simulation scoring of neuron explanations. Its CoSy simulation scores rate SPICE's cluster descriptions against baselines. The record's V4 'tests' link is therefore not supported.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors present SPICE as a generalizable, scalable attribution-clustering method that sets the number of clusters per neuron adaptively and outperforms PURE, LE and CPE on separability. They report distinct depth trajectories of polysemanticity in CNNs and ViTs. They treat polysemanticity as fundamental and argue interpretability should shift from single neurons to the concept clusters they encode.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes vision-model neurons by clustering attribution footprints and assessing concept separability and similarity distributions; it does not use the claimed Qwen3 neuron-pole audit procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported architectural and depth differences; threshold selection also changes cluster counts and within-cluster similarity, but those results do not measure V4’s claimed interpretable-neuron share.

fits_no_version.finding: Late ViT-B blocks have a multimodal subpopulation in attribution-similarity distributions: 43% of block-11 neurons have Dip p<0.05, and mean p falls to 0.28. ResNet-50 stays unimodal (p>0.9) at all depths. The authors read multimodality as polysemanticity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In ImageNet-trained ViTs, late-layer neurons more often show multimodal attribution footprints (a proxy for mixed concepts) than in ResNet-50.

fits_no_version.finding: SPICE concept-cluster counts per neuron: ResNet keeps many until a drop in the final blocks, while ViT declines gradually. In supplementary Figure 2, ViT yields more clusters than ResNet-50 at every threshold. Counts depend on the threshold p.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Attribution-cluster counts per vision neuron differ by architecture and depend on the clustering threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: Neuron #652 (ViT-B block 11) splits into unrelated clusters: snakeskin, penguins, two-wheelers. Upstream top-50 overlap is 18% for a neuron with unrelated concepts versus 42% for one with related concepts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Vision neurons combining related concepts share more upstream circuitry than those combining unrelated concepts.

fits_no_version.finding: In DINOv3 ViT-L fine-tuned on Food-101, 284 of 1,024 MLP neurons (about 28%) kept their original concept clusters.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning often repurposes pretrained vision neurons to new concepts.

record.peer_reviewed: European Conference on Computer Vision -- ECCV 2026
record.problems: The study concerns vision models rather than language models and does not report the claimed interpretable-neuron proportions. Architectural observations are descriptive, not causal tests of architecture, regularization, or tool quality. Several cluster-count trends are available only as figures without numerical values.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. Comparisons among clustering methods and their separability scores were left out because they evaluate method performance, not the proportion of interpretable neurons named in V4.

untested.parts: All: no Qwen3-32B audit and no pole shares.
All: vision models only, with no language models or MoE models and no scale range.
All: no InceptionV1 cat/car neuron and no test of pose or recursive generalization versus superposition.
All: no interpretable-neuron share by tool or architecture. No causal test of architecture, regularization or tool quality. No InceptionV1 estimate.
All: no neuron attribution graphs explaining behaviour and no replacement-model comparison.
All: no test of whether activating-example explanations predict firing on new inputs.
All: no simulation scoring of neuron explanations on new text. CoSy AUC/MAD here scores SPICE cluster descriptions against baselines.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V4 label (limits_scope) is removed: no row measures a share of interpretable neurons. The study's framing, that polysemanticity is pervasive and more prevalent in ViTs, runs against the spirit of V4. However, it rests on tool-defined measures, so it is recorded under fits_no_version rather than as a verdict. The separability and baseline comparisons were rightly left out.

versions.untested_parts: Qwen3-32B audit and the claimed proportions of poles with one job, two related jobs, or not-yet-understood jobs.
Language models, dense and mixture-of-experts language architectures, model scale up to trillions of parameters, and the claimed cross-model shares.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car example, shared pose feature, and recursive generalization versus superposition.

The study reports architectural differences in visual-model polysemanticity, but does not test the causal roles of architecture, regularization, or tool quality; measure the share of interpretable neurons; or estimate the stated InceptionV1-sized-model change from about 5% to about 99%.
Neuron-based attribution graphs, behavioral reconstruction, replacement models, and reconstruction error.
Whether explanations formed from activating examples predict firing on separate, held-out inputs.
Automated simulation-based scores for neuron explanations on new text.

relation.reason: Analyses individual vision neurons as units and treats polysemanticity as a premise. It does not test any version of the claim.

tranche.reason: Method paper (SPICE attribution clustering) that takes polysemanticity as given. Its Dip-test depth analysis justifies its thresholding design and does not measure a share of interpretable neurons.

source_check.notes: Dip-test p-values measure the multimodality of each neuron's attribution-similarity distribution in ImageNet vision models (ViT-B, ResNet-50), not the share of interpretable or one-job neurons. The main text (Fig. 7 discussion) says all models become 'distinctly bimodal' later, but Supp. Table 4 and Section 3 say ResNet-50 stays unimodal (p>0.9). The statement follows the supplement. The pack lists 25 of 29 rows. The statement also cites R26-R27, which were not listed; the text's ResNet-50 layers 14-15 (0.97±0.12, 0.98±0.09) match the statement.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Architectures show different polysemanticity trends: ResNet-50 is reported as unimodal across depths, while late ViT layers show a multimodal subpopulation; the study does not establish a general rise in interpretable-neuron share. Rows R1, R11-R12, R13-R27, R28-R29.
